# Pocket Positivity Trio

### Sunny the Sunflower · Waddle the Penguin · Spud the Potato

Three palm-sized amigurumi designed to slip into a coat pocket. They work up
fast — an evening or two for all three — and make excellent small gift add-ons,
party favours, or a gentle first project.

The trio shares one body: a **six-stitch sphere for Waddle**, a **six-stitch
cushion for Sunny**, and a **flat oval for Spud**. Once you have worked the
first toy, the other two will feel familiar.

---

## At a Glance

| | Sunny | Waddle | Spud |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | Flat six-petal flower | Pear-shaped penguin | Rounded potato |
| Finished size | about 3.0 cm (1.2 in) across the petals | about 3.8 cm (1.5 in) tall | about 2.7 cm (1.1 in) long |
| Yarn weight | #4 worsted | #4 worsted | #4 worsted |
| Hook | 3.5 mm (US E/4) | 3.5 mm (US E/4) | 3.5 mm (US E/4) |
| Time per toy | 20–30 minutes | 20–30 minutes | 25–35 minutes |

Sunny and Waddle have no separate pieces to sew. Spud is worked flat, then the
seam is closed in one stitch. All three are worked in continuous spiral rounds
with a stitch marker, so there is no slip stitch at the end of each round.

---

## Materials

- **Yarn:** worsted weight / #4 (about 250 m per 100 g). The three toys use
  roughly 8 m of yarn in total — under 4 g — so almost any scrap will do.
  - Sunny — golden yellow for the petals, chocolate brown for the center
  - Waddle — black, plus cream for the chest patch and yellow for the beak
  - Spud — warm tan
- **Hook:** 3.5 mm (US E/4)
- **Eyes:** 5 mm black safety eyes ×6 (or embroidery thread — see *Safety and
  selling*, below)
- **Fiberfill:** about 3 g in total for all three, or enough to fill each body
  firmly without lumps
- **Blunt tapestry needle**, stitch marker, scissors

---

## Gauge

Approximately **3.5 mm per stitch** and **3.2 mm per round** in single crochet
worked in the round with the stated yarn and hook. Amigurumi is normally worked
a half-size tighter than the yarn calls for.

This is a pocket-size set, so gauge matters: a single half-size difference
changes the finished size noticeably. Work a gauge swatch before you start.
The sizes in the table above are calculated from this gauge.

---

## Skill Level

**Easy / beginner-friendly.**

### Techniques you will use

1. **Magic ring** — the starting loop for Sunny's center and Waddle's body.
2. **Working in a continuous spiral** with a stitch marker, rather than joining
   each round.
3. **Invisible decreases** (see the note at the end of the pattern).
4. **Clusters worked into one stitch** — Sunny's petals. Three stitches are
   worked into a single stitch of the round below, which makes them stand out
   from the center.
5. **Slip stitch edging** between the petals, which flattens the joins.
6. **Oval base worked around a chain** — Spud's potato. You work along one side
   of a foundation chain, around the end, back along the other side, and round
   the other end, increasing at both ends.
7. **Sewing and embroidery** for Waddle's wings, chest and beak, and Sunny's
   center and face.

---

## Abbreviations (US terms)

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| MR | magic ring |
| sc | single crochet |
| hdc | half double crochet |
| inc | increase (2 sc in one stitch) |
| dec | invisible decrease |
| sl st | slip stitch |
| ch | chain |
| st(s) | stitch(es) |
| [...] x N | repeat the bracketed sequence N times |

---

# Sunny the Sunflower

A cheerful little face that works up in about twenty minutes. The brown center
is a small cushion, and nine petals are worked directly into it.

## Body — brown center (make 1)

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) |
| Rnd 2 | inc in each st around | (12) |
| Rnd 3 | [sc, inc] x6 | (18) |
| Rnd 4 | sc in each st around | (18) |
| Rnd 5 | [sc, dec] x6 | (12) |
| Rnd 6 | dec x6 — stuff the center firmly before closing | (6) |

Fasten off. Weave the tail through the front loops of the remaining 6 stitches,
pull tight to close, and weave in the end on the inside.

## Petals — yellow (make 1)

Join yellow with a slip stitch into any stitch of **Rnd 3** of the center.

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Petal rnd | [sl st in next st, (sc, hdc, sc) in next st] x9 | (36) |

Fasten off and weave in the end.

This repeat uses 2 stitches per petal — a slip stitch, then three stitches into
the next one — so **nine petals close the round exactly**. The slip stitch sits
in the valley between petals and makes them fan outward. Work this round
loosely, especially the three stitches in one stitch; if it pulls tight, step up
to a 4 mm hook for this round only and return to 3.5 mm afterwards.

## Face

Embroider a smiling mouth with black embroidery thread between Rnd 2 and Rnd 3
of the center. Add 5 mm safety eyes (or embroider them) **3 stitches apart** on
Rnd 2, centerd over the mouth.

> **Eye spacing.** At 3.5 mm per stitch, three stitches is about 10.5 mm between
> the eyes. Four stitches is about 14 mm, which on this 20 mm face leaves the
> 5 mm eyes almost touching the rim of the cushion. Use four stitches only if
> you are embroidering the eyes rather than inserting safety eyes.

---

# Waddle the Penguin

A pear-shaped body, a cream chest patch, two small wings and a beak. Only the
wings are sewn on.

## Body — black (make 1)

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) |
| Rnd 2 | inc in each st around | (12) |
| Rnd 3 | [sc, inc] x6 | (18) |
| Rnd 4–6 | sc in each st around, 3 rnd | (18) |
| Rnd 7 | [2 sc, inc] x6 | (24) |
| Rnd 8–9 | sc in each st around, 2 rnd | (24) |
| Rnd 10 | [2 sc, dec] x6 | (18) |
| Rnd 11 | [sc, dec] x6 | (12) |
| Rnd 12 | dec x6 — stuff firmly as you go | (6) |

Fasten off. Weave the tail through the remaining 6 stitches and pull tight to
close. Weave in the end.

## Wings — black (make 2)

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | 4 sc in MR | (4) |
| Rnd 2 | [sc, inc] x2 | (6) |
| Rnd 3–4 | sc in each st around, 2 rnd | (6) |

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail for sewing. Do not stuff.

## Chest patch — cream (make 1)

Work this small oval, which is sewn flat onto the front of the body:

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | ch 6, sc in 2nd ch from hook, 3 sc, 3 sc in last ch; working on the other side of the chain: 3 sc, 2 sc in last ch | (12) |
| Rnd 2 | inc, 3 sc, inc x3, 3 sc, inc x2 | (18) |

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail.

> **Check the round:** a chain of 6 closes at 12 stitches — two stitches for
> every chain, because the turning chain and the last chain each take a cluster.
> Rnd 2 uses 1 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 12 stitches and produces 18.

## Beak — yellow (make 1)

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | ch 2, 3 sc in 2nd ch from hook | (3) |
| Rnd 2 | inc x3 | (6) |
| Rnd 3 | sc in each st around | (6) |

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. The beak is tiny — work it with the tail end of
the yarn only, and do not stuff it.

## Face and assembly

1. Add 5 mm safety eyes **3 stitches apart** on Rnd 3, between Rnd 2 and Rnd 3.
   (As with Sunny, four stitches leaves the eyes almost at the edge of an
   18-stitch face.)
2. Sew the beak centerd directly between the eyes, angled slightly downward.
3. Sew the cream chest patch onto the front of the body, covering Rnds 4–8.
   Stitch along the top and bottom edges only so the middle can puff slightly.
4. Sew the two wings onto the sides at Rnd 6, angled backward as though the
   penguin were mid-waddle. Pin them first and check the angle before sewing.
5. Add a tiny blush of pink chalk or pastel on the cheeks with a cotton swab.
   Use it sparingly.

---

# Spud the Potato

A flat, slightly lumpy oval — the shape comes from the seam, not the stitching.
No stuffing is needed until the closing step.

## Body — warm tan (make 1)

**Foundation:** ch 7.

| Round | Instructions | Stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Rnd 1 | sc in 2nd ch from hook, 4 sc, 3 sc in last ch; working on the other side of the chain: 4 sc, 2 sc in last ch; place marker to join | (14) |
| Rnd 2 | inc, 4 sc, inc x3, 4 sc, inc x2 | (20) |
| Rnd 3–6 | sc in each st around, 4 rnd | (20) |
| Rnd 7 | [3 sc, dec] x4 | (16) |
| Rnd 8 | [2 sc, dec] x4 | (12) |
| Rnd 9 | [sc, dec] x4 | (8) |
| Rnd 10 | dec x4 — begin stuffing at Rnd 9 | (4) |

Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

**Closing the seam:** with the body flat, use the tail to whip stitch the
remaining opening closed. Sew along the flat top so the seam reads as the
potato's natural crease. Weave in the end on the inside.

## Face

Add 5 mm safety eyes (or embroider them) about **5 stitches apart** on the broad
side, around Rnd 4. Spud's face is the widest of the three at about 27 mm, so
four or five stitches both sit comfortably inside the edge — choose to taste.
Embroider a small open mouth below and between the eyes.

---

## Making a Bigger Trio

The three finished sizes above are worked in the round with #4 worsted on a
3.5 mm hook. If you want the toys noticeably larger, switch to a 3.5 mm hook
with **chunky or aran weight yarn**, or work #4 worsted held double:

- at about **4.5 mm per stitch** everything scales up by roughly 1.3×
- Sunny about **3.9 cm** across the petals
- Waddle about **4.9 cm** tall
- Spud about **3.5 cm** long

No stitch counts change — the same rounds give the same shapes at the new size.
Make a gauge swatch first, because yarns vary.

---

## Safety and Selling

**This set is not intended for children under 3.** Safety eyes are small parts
that can be pulled off and swallowed. Even with safety washers fitted, a
determined child can work an eye loose.

If you are making these for young children, **embroider the eyes and mouths with
yarn** instead of using safety eyes. Embroidered eyes look just as good at this
scale and remove the hazard entirely.

A note for sellers:

- **Do not market these as "baby-safe."** The term has no legal definition in
  toy safety, and using it as a listing filter invites a claim you cannot
  support. Toys sold to children in the EU must carry CE marking under EN 71,
  and in the United States must meet the CPSIA lead and phthalate limits and
  ASTM F963. Independent testing is the only way to know whether your toys
  meet those standards.
- Sell them instead as **adult collectibles, desk companions, or keychain
  charms** — the pocket-size format suits that framing well.
- Include a hang tag or listing line with your **materials, your name as maker,
  and "Not suitable for children under 3 years."**
- Stuff firmly and evenly. Lumpy or under-stuffed toys read as cheap and lose
  their shape within weeks.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Petal edges curl** | Use invisible decreases on Rnd 5 of Sunny's center and pull the closing round snugly. |
| **Petal round will not close** | Nine repeats of the petal sequence use exactly 18 stitches — two per repeat. Make sure you worked Rnd 3 to (18) and that you slip-stitched once per repeat. |
| **The toys come out smaller than the sizes in the table** | Your tension is tighter than 3.5 mm per stitch. Work up half a hook size at a time, or hold #4 worsted double — see *Making a Bigger Trio*. |
| **The toys come out larger than the sizes in the table** | Your tension is looser than 3.5 mm per stitch. Drop to a 3 mm hook. |
| **Sunny's petals sit flat instead of standing out** | Work the three stitches in one stitch loosely, or step up to a 4 mm hook for the petal round only. |
| **Waddle's wings flop** | Sew them at Rnd 6 and catch a stitch of the body with each pass. |
| **Spud's seam shows** | Whip stitch along the flat top so the seam reads as a crease, and stuff evenly before closing. |
| **Eyes sit too close to the edge** | On Sunny and Waddle use three stitches apart, not four. |

---

## Invisible Decrease

An invisible decrease (inv dec) produces a flatter join than a standard
decrease, which matters at this scale.

1. Insert your hook under the **front loop only** of the next stitch.
2. Insert your hook under the **front loop only** of the stitch after that.
   You should have three loops on the hook.
3. Yarn over and pull through the first two loops.
4. Yarn over and pull through both remaining loops.

---

## Care

Spot clean with a damp cloth and mild soap; do not machine wash. Keep away from
heat. Surface-fluff any pulled loops with a clean pet slicker brush or a toothbrush.

---

*Pocket Positivity Trio — US crochet terms. Three palm-sized amigurumi: Sunny the
Sunflower, Waddle the Penguin, and Spud the Potato.*
